inputs.hard_hit_definition: ctrl-llm gold_rank==0 AND ctrl-cas gold_rank!=0 on the hard tier, seed 42 (analyze_hits.py); 1,401 of 15,000 queries

slice_definitions.v1_excluded: anchor matched by the v1 exact-text mapping, so its corpus id was dropped by the always-on training gate -- the paper's 'guaranteed clean' set (8,761 queries)
slice_definitions.v1_excluded_strict: v1_excluded and no v2 twin of the anchor appears in either arm's rows
slice_definitions.v1_excluded_leaked_dupe: v1_excluded but a corpus-internal duplicate/twin WAS trained (v1 kept only the first id per text)
slice_definitions.leaked_llm / leaked_cas: not v1-matched, has a v2 twin, and at least one twin id is in that arm's rows -> the arm trained on this query's own text
slice_definitions.notleaked_llm / notleaked_cas: not v1-matched, has v2 twins, none in that arm's rows -- the matched comparison population
slice_definitions.leaked_either: not v1-matched and leaked into either arm
slice_definitions.untrained_twin: not v1-matched, has v2 twins, none trained in either arm
slice_definitions.no_corpus_twin: no corpus twin under any v2 rule (79 anchors)
slice_definitions.strict_clean_all: no v2 twin of the anchor is in either arm's rows -- the strictest clean slice

scopes.trained: leakage judged against source_ids the weights saw (5% dev split removed)
scopes.used: leakage judged against every gated row of the arm's data file -- the review's definition

document_side_leakage_audit.reading: normalization-equal, not merely similar. ::orig docs are the benchmark's 1,668 organic originals (99.8% are corpus problems), so any corpus-sampled negative can reproduce one; ::nm:: hits are hard-negative documents; the handful of ::eq:: (gold) hits sit mostly in the NEGATIVES column, where the effect is to push the gold document away -- conservative for the LLM arm, not favourable.

reviewer_cross_check.quantity: seed-42 arm gap on v1-excluded (guaranteed-clean) slice
seed-42 ctrl-llm easy R@1 on leaked slice
seed-42 ctrl-llm easy R@1 on untrained-twin slice
gap points attributable to leakage (LLM arm only)
hard-tier P(recipe hit) on leaked slice, %
hard-tier P(recipe hit) on clean slices, %
% of ctrl-llm rows whose anchor is benchmark-query text
